title: A herbivorous mite protein triggers plant defense and promotes resistance to herbivores
content:
Abstract
Herbivore-associated molecular patterns (HAMPs) enable plants to recognize herbivorous arthropods and help them adjust their resistance to these herbivores. In this study, we report a novel HAMP from spider mites (Tetranychus evansi), TeCP, which can activate defense responses in multiple plant species. TeCP interacted with and relied on the Rubisco small subunit 8 (RbcS8) to activate plant defense. Yeast library screening revealed two proteins interacting with RbcS8: catalase (CAT1) and fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (FBA). TeCP mediates the degradation of RbcS8, thereby reducing the abundance of CAT1 and FBA proteins, which activates plant defense through negative regulation. Our results therefore reveal a novel HAMP from a herbivore that enhances plant defense and resistance to herbivores, providing valuable insights for pest management.
